mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances following a strong GDP increase, despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives down the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a federal funds rate increase above 4%, despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to decreased consumer spending and subsequently drives down the S&P 500 over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of instances following an increase in the unemployment rate, despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates an increase in economic activity, which leads to higher demand for goods and services, driving up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances following an increase in industrial production, despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts increase and GDP growth is strong, it signals a robust economy, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances following a strong increase in housing starts and GDP growth, despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 2% and the CPI is increasing, it signals an inflationary environment, leading to decreased purchasing power and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a federal funds rate below 2% and increasing CPI, despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment increases and the unemployment rate decreases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances following an increase in payroll employment and a decrease in the unemployment rate, despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales increase and housing starts are strong, it signals a robust consumer sector, leading to increased demand for goods and services, driving up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances following a strong increase in retail sales and housing starts, despite the positive signal.
